newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM asks king for pardon for prince.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM asks king for pardon for prince.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh has formally requested a royal pardon for exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh in a move likely to heat up a simmering political dispute.
The request for a pardon was made to King Norodom Sihanouk in a letter from Ranariddh dated Wednesday but released on Thursday.
It is the latest development in a complex tangle over the fate of Sirivudh, who was sentenced for an alleged plot to assassinate second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Sirivudh, half-brother of the king, was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment in absentia. He was exiled to France nearly one year ago to avoid imprisonment.
Sirivudh has since vowed to return to Cambodia, angering Hun Sen, drawing support from Ranariddh and inspiring caution on the part of the king, who brokered his exile.

Opposition leader Sam Rainsy, who heads the Khmer Nation Party, has also weighed in on the issue. On Thursday, he released a statement urging the return of Sirivudh and calling the prince a victim of politics.
Hun Sen last week threatened to call out troops and tanks to prevent Sirivudh's return, but later said he would welcome Sirivudh with flowers if he were given an amnesty by the king.
On Wednesday, the king said he would not grant amnesty to Sirivudh without the approval of Hun Sen.
An adviser to Hun Sen told Reuters on Thursday that the decision on amnesty is up to the king.
Sirivudh has said he will not change his plans to return to Cambodia, though he would not reveal the date of his return.
